fieldMarks: Rams carry massive curled horns; ewes have shorter, slender, slightly curved horns
Rams under about 3 years resemble ewes; yearling rams are hard to tell from ewes
behavior: Rams live in bands apart from ewe groups except during the late November–early December rut
Rams clash horns to establish rank
Moves to higher elevations in spring and lower in fall; very loyal to seasonal home ranges
Travels many miles to mineral licks in spring
habitat: Relatively dry mountain country: open alpine ridges, meadows and steep slopes next to rugged cliffs used as escape terrain.
range: Brooks Range, Alaska Range and Kenai Peninsula of Alaska, and the Mackenzie and northern Rocky Mountains of Yukon, the Northwest Territories and northern British Columbia; many southern populations are isolated.

lookalikes.name: Mountain goat
lookalikes.howToTell: Sometimes confused; Dall sheep prefer drier country and do not occur in Southeast Alaska.
